events.title: Genghis Khan – The World of the Mongols
events.description: Major exhibition on the Mongol empire with archaeological treasures from Mongolia, many shown outside the country for the first time.

events.title: Himmel unter Berlin Vol. III
events.description: Immersive installation labyrinth in a former engine factory, open on three weekends in October; location revealed 48 hours before the visit.

events.title: Long Night of the Manufacturers
events.venue: Various workshops in Mitte, Wedding, Moabit, Tiergarten, Gesundbrunnen and Hansaviertel
events.description: First Long Night of Manufacturers: workshops, studios and backyards open their doors with tours, tastings and live demonstrations.

events.title: Festival of Lights
events.description: Light art and video installations illuminate Berlin's landmarks under the theme 'Colours of Love', with music and performances.

events.title: Long Night of Families
events.description: 16th Long Night of Families with theatre, sport, picture-book cinema, concerts and experiments across the city, mostly free.

events.title: PEOPLE Festival
events.description: Improvised festival with 180 international musicians in 40 studios; 200 concerts across eleven stages at Funkhaus on the weekend.

events.title: Berlin Food Week
events.description: Food festival bringing together chefs, restaurateurs, start-ups and producers, with the House of Food at Bikini Berlin and OkSoberfest.

events.title: CLUB CULTURE DAY
events.venue: Various clubs and venues across Berlin
events.description: Seventh edition under the theme STAY CORE, combining a cultural award for clubs and collectives with a week-long festival.

events.title: Jazzfest Berlin 2026
events.description: Four days of contemporary avant-garde jazz with the Anthony Braxton Septet, Immanuel Wilkins Quartet, ganavya and many premieres.

events.title: Kazuki Yamada's Inaugural Concert with the DSO
events.description: Kazuki Yamada's inaugural concert as DSO chief conductor with Ives, Grieg with Alice Sara Ott, Anna Clyne and Debussy, plus Maja Göpel.
